content.heading: ✅ Q1: Choose the Correct Statement for Each of the Following
content.leadHtml: Each question is immediately followed by its solution card.

content.problemHtml:
The effective value of the alternating voltage in an AC circuit equals

  • a- \(1.5\,V_m\)
  • b- \(0.707\,V_m\)
  • c- \(0.636\,V_m\)
  • d- \(\sqrt{2}\,V_m\)

steps.note: The effective value of an alternating voltage is always \(V_e=0.707\,V_m\), a fixed relation we studied in the first lesson.

content.problemHtml:
Power consumption in a pure ohmic resistance is

  • a- Real
  • b- As large as possible
  • c- Zero
  • d- None of the above

steps.note: A pure ohmic resistance consumes real power that appears as heat, unlike a pure inductor and a pure capacitor, which consume no real power.

content.problemHtml:
To step up the alternating voltage we use

  • a- A motor
  • b- A generator
  • c- A coil
  • d- An electrical transformer

steps.note: A step-up transformer is the device used to raise the alternating voltage, relying on the principle of mutual induction.

solution.final: ✓ Correct answer: d — An electrical transformer
solution.label: Solution

content.problemHtml:
In a series AC circuit containing an inductor, a resistance, and a capacitor, the value of the impedance relative to the resistance is

  • a- Greater than it.
  • b- Less than it.
  • c- Equal to it.
  • d- None of the above.

steps.note: Since \(Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}\), the second term under the root is always positive or zero (at resonance), so Z is greater than or equal to R, and in general (except at resonance) Z is greater than R.

solution.final: ✓ Correct answer: a — Greater than it
solution.label: Solution

content.problemHtml:
The value of the power factor in an AC electrical circuit containing an inductor only is

  • a- Zero.
  • b- Greater than one.
  • c- Less than one.
  • d- None of the above.

steps.note: In a pure inductor, the voltage leads the current by an angle of 90°, so \(\cos90°=0\), meaning the power factor equals zero.

content.problemHtml:
The two terminals of the secondary coil in the electrical transformer are connected to

  • a- The source.
  • b- The device (the load).
  • c- The core.
  • d- None of the above.

steps.note: The primary coil is connected to the alternating source, while the secondary coil is connected to the device (the load).

solution.final: ✓ Correct answer: b — The device (the load)
solution.label: Solution

content.problemHtml:
One of the causes of power loss in the electrical circuit is

  • a- Eddy currents.
  • b- Connecting the transformer in series.
  • c- The large size of the transformer.
  • d- The presence of a magnetic field.

steps.note: Among the causes of power loss in the electrical transformer: the eddy currents generated in its iron core, in addition to heat losses in the wires and hysteresis losses.

content.heading: ✏️ Q2: Fill in the Following Blanks

content.problemHtml: There is ---------- power consumption in a pure ohmic resistance.
✓ Real (actual)
The ---------- does not depend on frequency in an AC circuit.
✓ The (pure) ohmic resistance
Inductive reactance is measured in units of ----------.
✓ The ohm (Ω)
Impedance is considered a ---------- quantity.
✓ Directional (vector)
It is more economical to transmit electrical power at a high ---------- and a low ----------.
✓ High voltage · low current
The transformer is considered a ---------- device only.
✓ Alternating current
To reduce the phase-difference angle between the voltage and current at electrical power transmission stations, we use ---------- connected in parallel.
✓ Capacitors
What is the difference between how a capacitor behaves in a DC circuit and in an AC circuit?

steps.note: In a DC circuit, the capacitor behaves like an open switch shortly after it is fully charged (no current flows). In an AC circuit, however, it behaves like a closed switch, since it charges and discharges alternately every quarter cycle, so the ammeter registers a continuous current despite the insulator between its plates.

solution.final: ✓ Open switch in DC — closed switch (periodic charge and discharge) in AC
solution.label: Answer

content.label: Q3

content.problemHtml: What is the meaning of the effective value of an alternating current? Write the relation between this value and the maximum value of the current.

steps.note: The effective value of an alternating current is the equivalent thermal value of direct current that produces the same amount of heat in a given resistance over the same time that the alternating current produces in it. Its relation to the maximum value: \(I_e=0.707\,I_m\).

content.label: Q4

content.problemHtml: How can a resistance, an inductor, and a capacitor, each placed in one of three similar boxes, be distinguished when each is connected separately to a battery, wires, and a light bulb?

steps.note: With a battery (direct current), wires, and a bulb: the box in which the bulb lights up steadily and continuously contains a resistance or an inductor (because \(X_L=0\) with direct current, so the inductor behaves like an ordinary resistance). The box in which the bulb does not light up at all (or flashes momentarily then goes out) contains a capacitor, because it behaves like an open switch once it is fully charged in a DC circuit.

solution.final: ✓ The capacitor is identified by the bulb going out (open switch); distinguishing the resistance from the inductor requires a variable-frequency AC source to observe the effect of X_L
solution.label: Answer

content.label: Q5

content.problemHtml: What is the power factor in each of the following: 1- The resistance. 2- The inductor. 3- The capacitor?

steps.note: 1- Pure resistance: phase difference = zero, so \(\cos\emptyset=\cos0°=1\).
2- Pure inductor: phase difference = 90°, so \(\cos\emptyset=\cos90°=0\).
3- Pure capacitor: phase difference = 90° (in the opposite direction), so \(\cos\emptyset=\cos90°=0\).

content.label: Q6

content.problemHtml: Why is the transformer considered an AC device?

steps.note: Because the operation of the transformer relies on the principle of mutual induction, which requires a continuous change in the magnetic flux; and this change occurs only with a current that varies in magnitude and direction (alternating), since the transformer contains no automatic switch to make that happen with a constant direct current.

solution.final: ✓ It relies on mutual induction, which requires a continuously varying magnetic flux, and this is achieved only with alternating current
solution.label: Answer

content.label: Q7

content.problemHtml: What are the power losses in the transformer?

steps.note: 1- Part of the electrical energy is lost as heat in the wires of the two coils. 2- Part of it is lost as heat generated in the transformer's core due to eddy currents. 3- Part of it is lost as hysteresis in the iron core material.

solution.final: ✓ Heat in the wires · eddy currents in the core · hysteresis in the core material
solution.label: Answer

content.label: Q8

content.problemHtml: What type of transformer is connected in load-supply areas?

steps.note: A step-down transformer is connected in load-supply areas, to lower the high voltage used in transmission to a safe voltage suitable for the consumer.

content.label: Q9

content.problemHtml: An AC circuit contains a pure ohmic resistance, in which the alternating current ranges between \((-10,\ +10)\) and the alternating voltage ranges between \((-14.14,\ +14.14)\). Calculate: 1- The effective current. 2- The effective voltage. 3- The value of the resistance.
content.label: 📝 Problem (1)

given: \( I_m = 10\ \text{A} \) — the maximum current value (ranges between −10 and +10)

steps.note: 1- We apply the relation for the effective value of the current
2- We apply the relation for the effective value of the voltage
3- We apply Ohm's law using the effective values (or the maximum values; the ratio is the same)

solution.label: Detailed Solution

content.problemHtml: A coil is connected to a source of alternating voltage with frequency \(\left(\dfrac{500}{\pi}\ \text{Hz}\right)\), and the inductive reactance value becomes \((125\ \Omega)\). Calculate the inductance of the coil.
content.label: 📝 Problem (2)

solution.required: The inductance of the coil L.

steps.note: We apply the inductive-reactance relation and rearrange it to find L

solution.label: Detailed Solution

content.problemHtml: A capacitor is connected to an AC source. If the capacitance of the capacitor is \(\left(\dfrac{100}{\pi}\ \mu F\right)\) and the capacitive reactance is \((100\ \Omega)\), calculate the frequency of the electrical circuit.
content.label: 📝 Problem (3)

steps.note: We apply the capacitive-reactance relation and rearrange it to find f

content.problemHtml: A resistance of \((3\ \Omega)\) is connected in series with an inductor of self-inductance \((50\ \text{mH})\) and a source of alternating voltage with frequency \(\left(\dfrac{40}{\pi}\ \text{Hz}\right)\), and the circuit current is \((2\ \text{A})\). Calculate the source voltage.
content.label: 📝 Problem (4)

steps.note: We first calculate the inductive reactance
We calculate the impedance, then apply Ohm's law to find the voltage

content.problemHtml: A capacitor of capacitance \((200\ \mu F)\) is connected in series with an ohmic resistance of \((40\ \Omega)\) to an AC electrical source of frequency \(\left(\dfrac{250}{3\pi}\ \text{Hz}\right)\). If the power consumed in the circuit is \((1000\ \text{W})\), calculate the source voltage.
content.label: 📝 Problem (5)

steps.note: We calculate the capacitive reactance and the impedance
We find the circuit current from the power consumed \((P=I_T^2R)\), then apply Ohm's law to find the voltage

content.problemHtml: If the power of the primary coil in an electrical transformer equals \((1000\ \text{W})\) and the power of the secondary coil is \((900\ \text{W})\). Calculate: 1- The power lost in the transformer. 2- The efficiency of the transformer.
content.label: 📝 Problem (6)

given: \( P_1 = 1000\ \text{W} \) — the power of the primary coil
\( P_2 = 900\ \text{W} \) — the power of the secondary coil

steps.note: 1- Power lost = power of the primary coil − power of the secondary coil
2- We apply the transformer efficiency relation

solution.label: Detailed Solution

questions.question: The effective value of the alternating current equals:
questions.explain: \(I_e=0.707\,I_m\), a relation based on the equal thermal effect between alternating and direct current.

questions.question: The voltage of a pure inductor relative to its current:
questions.explain: The voltage of a pure inductor leads its current by a phase-difference angle of 90°.

questions.question: The current of a pure capacitor relative to its voltage:
questions.explain: The current of a pure capacitor leads its voltage by a phase-difference angle of 90°.

questions.question: The impedance of a series RLC circuit is calculated from:
questions.explain: \(Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}\), where \(X_L\) and \(X_C\) are subtracted first (since they are 180° out of phase) and the result is then combined vectorially with R.

questions.question: At electrical resonance \((X_L=X_C)\), the properties of the circuit are:
questions.explain: At resonance, \((X_L-X_C)\) vanishes, so \(Z=R\) only, meaning the properties of the circuit become purely resistive (the current and voltage are in the same phase).

questions.question: A transformer with a turns ratio of \(N_2/N_1=1/12\) is:
questions.explain: Since \(N_2/N_1=1/12\), which is less than 1, this transformer steps down the voltage.

summary.heading: 📋 Chapter Four Summary
items: Pure resistance: zero phase difference; pure inductor: voltage leads by 90°; pure capacitor: current leads by 90°.
The transformer: \(N_2/N_1=V_2/V_1\), \(\eta=(P_2/P_1)\times100\%\); step-up at generation, step-down at the load, to reduce transmission loss.
